To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the protein A-god technique is a useful tool for immunocytochemical studies of the teleost GH.
the protein A-golds were located on secretogranules of the GH cells in the tilapia pitutary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of protein A-gold to the immunocytochemistry on the ultrastructural level.
the application of the gold-labeling technique to the immunocytochemistry in fish.
the development of the immunocytochemical techniques for the study of the teleoset pituitary hormones.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the protein A-gol technique for immunoelectron microscopy of the tilapia GH is useful for the detection of the antigenic sites of the hormone in the pituitary cells and for the study of the ultrastructure and cytochemical properties of these cells.
the protein A-god technique is an efficient method for immunocytochemical studies on the pituitary gland of the teleosts.
protein A-gold method is an effective tool for the localization of intracellular antigen in the pituitary cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the tilapia GH cells are located in the proximal and middle pars distalis, and the cells in these two regions are morphologically different.
the tilapia pituatory cells are classified into two cell types on the basis of ultrastructural characteristics: one is the GH cell and the other is the non-GH cell.

the tilapia pitutary GH cells were identified and the ultrastructural features were described in the proximal and the distal pars distalis of tilapia pituitaries, which is a valuable information for the future study of pituitary GH cells of teleosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the protein A-golds are useful for detecting intracellular antigenicities in the pituitary gland of the teleost fish.
it is possible to use the protein A-golds technique in the immunoelectronic microscopic study of teleost GH.
